newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends down sharply, further losses seen.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends down sharply, further losses seen.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures closed sharply lower on steady trade selling amid a dearth of buying in what many analysts believe to be the beginning of a major downtrend.
After retracing recent losses and climbing to a high of 73.65 cents a lb Thursday, July cotton sank to a three-day low of 72.40 cents today. It fetched 72.30 cents May 27.
July's close below key 73.00 cents is expected to encourage follow-through selling on Monday, said analysts who pegged major technical support at 65.90 cents.
"If we take that out there is no support until the 50s (cents per lb)," Jim Cordier, an analyst with Allendale, said.
July finished 1.11 cents lower at 72.45 cents after trading from 73.50 to 72.40 cents. New-crop December closed down 0.58 at 75.03, with the rest 0.80 to 0.50 lower.

Fundamental pressure came from market talk that cotton merchant Allenberg would bring as many as 150,000 480-lb bales of Texas-style cotton to the board, adding to the already hefty 200,154 bales on the board as of May 29.
Analysts said merchants may now prefer Memphis cotton due to a narrowing of the price between low-grade Texas cotton and high-grade Memphis growths.
At the same time China, a major buyer of U.S. cotton has become less interest in Texas cotton.

"The difference between Memhpis and Texas is narrow enough that an exporter may buy Memphis for export purposes," an analyst said, adding that Allenberg has been a noted seller on the floor, for the past two weeks.
Increasing certificated stocks would weigh heavily on the July contract, while the next planted acreage report, released in late June, will influence new-crop December futures, analysts said.
A disappointing export and sales report sparked early selling, which continued to erode gains amid a lack of buying, floor sources said.
An estimated 13,000 lots changed hands on the day, compared with Thursday's official 13,652 lots.
